advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Derive the exclude patterns in _ignore_lock_artifacts from lock.WRITE_LOCK_NAME / lock.MKDIR_LOCK_NAME (with a trailing '/' on the dir) instead of hardcoded literals, and/or extend a drift-guard test to cover this fallback.
evidence: tests/interfaces/store/test_lock_gitignored.py:11: the seeded ignore entries 'must stay consistent with the defining name constants (no drifting literals)' — but that test targets `tickets:.gitignore`, not `_ignore_lock_artifacts`'s info/exclude output
advisory.finding: _ignore_lock_artifacts hardcodes the lock artifact ignore patterns ('.ticket-write.lock', '.ticket-write.lock.d/') as string literals instead of deriving them from lock.WRITE_LOCK_NAME / lock.MKDIR_LOCK_NAME. The existing drift-guard regression (tests/interfaces/store/test_lock_gitignored.py) only pins the seeded .gitignore generator, not this new info/exclude fallback, so if the lock file/dir names change, this fallback will silently write stale patterns and lock artifacts will surface as untracked in an implicit-legacy store.
advisory.suggested_fix: Reference the constants: `for pattern in (_lock.WRITE_LOCK_NAME, f"{_lock.MKDIR_LOCK_NAME}/")` and import them alongside the existing lazy `_lock` import.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test forcing `_ignore_lock_artifacts` to fail (strict → PushDeliveryError reason 'stage-failed'; default → best-effort warning + no lock acquisition) to cover the pre-lock early-exit branch.
evidence: push.py:546-549 distinct detail 'could not exclude tracker lock artifacts from staging' and early return before `with _lock.write_lock(...)`
search of tests/unit for `_ignore_lock_artifacts` returned (no matches)
advisory.finding: The `_ignore_lock_artifacts(canonical)` == False branch (push.py:545-549) is untested: it emits reason 'stage-failed' with a distinct detail ('could not exclude tracker lock artifacts from staging') and returns/raises BEFORE the write lock is acquired — an observably different early-exit path from the other stage-failed cases. No test forces this failure (e.g. by monkeypatching `push._ignore_lock_artifacts` or the underlying rev-parse/exclude write to fail), so a regression that acquired the lock anyway, mis-classified the reason, or staged the lock artifacts would go undetected.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend the fault-injection parametrization to include a `status`-failure case asserting reason 'stage-failed' (strict) and best-effort content retention (default).
evidence: test_commit_and_push_tickets_branch_heldout.py failing_git injects only when `args[0] == phase`, so status is never made to fail
advisory.finding: The `git status --porcelain` failure branch (push.py:567-572, reason 'stage-failed') is untested. The parametrized fault-injection test only injects failures for phase in {'add','commit'} (`if args and args[0] == phase`), so `status` always returns rc 0; the status-failed classification path (strict raise vs default warning + content retention) is never exercised.
